description: Warm-blooded furry animals with grasping hands forward-facing eyes large brains and complex social behaviour. Often arboreal.
examples: Sumatran orangutan | Bornean orangutan | Javan gibbon | Proboscis monkey | Javan slow loris

description: Warm-blooded furry animals with four sturdy legs and heavy body mass. Typically hooved or padded. Herbivorous or omnivorous.
examples: Sumatran elephant | Javan rhinoceros | Sumatran rhinoceros | Anoa | Banteng

description: Warm-blooded furry animals with four legs and compact body. Includes carnivores and omnivores with clawed or padded feet.
examples: Sumatran tiger | Clouded leopard | Sun bear | Flat-headed cat | Binturong

description: Warm-blooded mammals fully adapted to ocean life. Streamlined body with flippers and no hind limbs. Breathe air at the surface.
examples: Dugong | Irrawaddy dolphin | Blue whale | Spinner dolphin | Bryde's whale

description: The only mammals capable of true powered flight. Winged forelimbs with thin membrane stretched between elongated fingers. Mostly nocturnal.
examples: Sulawesi flying fox | Dayak fruit bat | Blanford's fruit bat | Horseshoe bat | Sunda flying lemur

description: Birds with vestigial non-functional wings. Powerful legs built for running. Large heavy body with dense feathers.
examples: Northern cassowary | Dwarf cassowary | Southern cassowary | Biak scrubfowl | New Guinea scrubfowl

description: Birds with fully developed wings capable of sustained flight. Lightweight hollow bones. Diverse in size shape and colour.
examples: Bali myna | Helmeted hornbill | Maleo | Yellow-crested cockatoo | Bird of paradise

description: Cold-blooded scaly animals with four legs and a long tail. Tongue used for sensing. Move in a low sprawling posture.
examples: Komodo dragon | Flying lizard | Borneo earless monitor | Green tree monitor | Sailfin lizard

description: Cold-blooded reptiles enclosed in a bony shell fused to the spine. Flippers for marine species or clawed legs for land species. Very slow-moving.
examples: Hawksbill sea turtle | Green sea turtle | Leatherback sea turtle | Pig-nosed turtle | Olive ridley turtle

description: Legless cold-blooded reptiles with an elongated flexible body covered in overlapping scales. Forked tongue for chemosensing.
examples: King cobra | Reticulated python | Javan spitting cobra | Brongersma's short-tailed python | Indonesian rat snake

description: Large semi-aquatic cold-blooded reptiles with armoured skin long powerful jaws and webbed feet. Ambush predators.
examples: Saltwater crocodile | False gharial | New Guinea crocodile | Siamese crocodile | Freshwater crocodile

description: Cold-blooded animals with moist smooth skin. No tail in adult stage. Long powerful hind legs for jumping. Begin life as aquatic tadpoles.
examples: Javan gliding frog | Bornean flat-headed frog | Huia cavitympanum | Wallace's flying frog | Microhyla borneensis

description: Aquatic vertebrates with fins and gills adapted to rivers lakes and streams. Bony skeleton with lateral line sensory system.
examples: Asian arowana | Mahseer | Boeseman's rainbowfish | Toman snakehead | Clown loach

description: Aquatic vertebrates with fins and gills adapted to saltwater ocean environments. Highly varied in body shape size and colouration.
examples: Whale shark | Napoleon wrasse | Manta ray | Sawfish | Bumphead parrotfish

description: Six-legged animals with three body segments exoskeleton and often wings. Largest animal group by species count.
examples: Wallace's golden birdwing | Queen Alexandra's birdwing | Atlas moth | Rajah Brooke's birdwing | Javan rhinoceros beetle

description: Soft-bodied animals often protected by a hard shell. Includes filter feeders sedentary reef builders and slow-moving grazers.
examples: Giant clam | Black coral | Nautilus | Fluted giant clam | Chambered nautilus

description: Large woody plant with a single upright trunk that branches high up into a wide leafy canopy. Dominates the rainforest upper layer.
examples: Borneo ironwood | Ramin | Kapur | Meranti | Ebony

description: Tall unbranched trunk topped with a crown of long arching fronds. Monocot with no secondary woody growth.
examples: Arenga palm | Pigafetta palm | Livistona palm | Salak palm | Gebang palm

description: Ancient cone-bearing plant with a stout low trunk and a crown of stiff pinnate leaves radiating outward. Produces cones not flowers.
examples: Cycas rumphii | Cycas javana | Cycas papuana | Cycas revoluta | Cycas elongata

description: Woody tree or shrub growing in coastal tidal zones with distinctive visible prop roots or stilt roots emerging from the water or mud.
examples: Rhizophora mucronata | Bruguiera gymnorrhiza | Sonneratia alba | Avicennia marina | Xylocarpus granatum

description: Woody multi-stemmed plant shorter than a tree with branches starting near the base. Dense bushy form with no dominant single trunk.
examples: Rhododendron variesgatum | Gardenia tubifera | Psychotria viridis | Melastoma malabathricum | Ixora javanica

description: Non-self-supporting plant with slender flexible stems that trails or twines around other structures to reach light. Includes spiny rattans.
examples: Calamus manan | Daemonorops draco | Bauhinia kockiana | Gnetum gnemon | Flagellaria indica

description: Grass-like plant with narrow blade-shaped leaves and jointed hollow or pithy stems. Grows in clumps or spreading mats.
examples: Dendrocalamus asper | Gigantochloa atroviolacea | Schizostachyum lima | Imperata cylindrica | Oryza rufipogon

description: Low-growing non-woody soft-stemmed plant rooted in soil. Small to medium in size staying close to the forest floor.
examples: Begonia multangula | Impatiens platypetala | Zingiber spectabile | Amomum cardamomum | Tacca integrifolia

description: Large soft-stemmed plant producing either a single massive compound leaf on a thick stalk or a giant hooded spathe flower. Dramatic in scale.
examples: Titan arum | Amorphophallus paeoniifolius | Colocasia gigantea | Alocasia macrorrhizos | Amorphophallus muelleri

description: Plant rooted in or freely floating on still or slow-moving freshwater. Leaves often flat and broad sitting on or just below the surface.
examples: Victoria amazonica | Nelumbo nucifera | Nymphaea lotus | Barclaya motleyi | Cryptocoryne affinis

description: Spore-bearing vascular plant with feathery or strap-like fronds that uncurl from a tight coil when young. Produces no flowers or seeds.
examples: Cyathea contaminans | Dipteris conjugata | Angiopteris evecta | Platycerium bifurcatum | Asplenium nidus

description: Flowering plant with highly distinctive bilateral flowers often patterned or coloured to attract pollinators. Roots may be fleshy and aerial.
examples: Grammatophyllum speciosum | Paphiopedilum rothschildianum | Coelogyne pandurata | Vanda tricolor | Bulbophyllum beccarii

description: Carnivorous plant producing modified leaves shaped into hanging pitcher or jug-like traps filled with digestive fluid to capture insects.
examples: Nepenthes rajah | Nepenthes lowii | Nepenthes villosa | Nepenthes truncata | Nepenthes gymnamphora

description: Plant that grows on the surface of another plant using it only for physical support. Has aerial roots or specialised structures to absorb moisture from air.
examples: Platycerium superbum | Dischidia major | Hoya imperialis | Drynaria quercifolia | Asplenium australasicum

description: Plant with no visible stem or leaves. Appears solely as an enormous single flower emerging directly from host roots or forest floor litter.
examples: Rafflesia arnoldii | Rafflesia patma | Rafflesia keithii | Balanophora fungosa | Rafflesia tuan-mudae
